---
title: TanStack Start
description: Type-safe environment variables for TanStack Start with the VITE_ prefix.
icon: TanStack
---

TanStack Start builds with Vite, so use the root `zod-config` export with `clientPrefix: "VITE_"`.

## Define the schema

```ts title="src/env.ts"
import { loadEnvConfig } from 'zod-config';
import { z } from 'zod';

export const env = loadEnvConfig({
  clientPrefix: 'VITE_',
  server: {
    DATABASE_URL: z.url(),
  },
  client: {
    VITE_APP_NAME: z.string(),
  },
  runtimeEnv: import.meta.env,
});
```

Client code can only read `VITE_`-prefixed variables. On the server, `server` variables are read from `runtimeEnv` first, then `process.env`. TanStack Start loads your `.env` files automatically.

## Validate when Vite starts

By default, the environment is validated when `env.ts` is first imported. To stop `vite dev` and `vite build` on a missing or invalid variable, add the [`zodConfigEnv` plugin](/docs/env/vite#validate-when-vite-starts) to `vite.config.ts`:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import { zodConfigEnv } from 'zod-config/vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [zodConfigEnv(), tanstackStart()],
});
```

## Read server variables in server functions

Read `server` variables inside `createServerFn` handlers (or server routes and middleware). Route loaders also run in the browser, where server values are never available, so reading one there throws.

```ts
import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start';
import { env } from './env';

export const getUsers = createServerFn().handler(async () => {
  const db = connect(env.DATABASE_URL); // your database client; runs on the server only
  return db.users.findMany();
});
```

A loader that needs server data calls the server function.

## Runtimes that inject variables per request

`loadEnvConfig` reads the environment once, when `env.ts` is first imported. On runtimes that inject variables per request, such as Cloudflare Workers, TanStack Start's docs recommend reading `process.env` inside each handler instead of at module scope. Check how your deployment target provides variables before relying on a module-level `env`.
